[[File:Deepseek chat.png|thumbnail|When one chats with an [[LLM]], the LLM repeatedly executes [[forward pass]] to generate a response, often token by token.]]
A '''forward pass''' of an [[artificial neural network (ANN)]], also called '''inference''', is the process of obtaining an output $f_\theta(X)$ based on input $X$.

== Stages ==

Common stages of a '''forward pass''' include:

* '''[[tokenisation (machine learning)|Tokenisation]]''' and '''[[token embedding (machine learning)|Token embedding]]''', to convert raw input into real vectors.
* '''Computation'''
** in a simple [[ANN]]: via [[feedforward algorithm]];
** in a [[Transformer]]: via multiple layers of [[self-attention]], [[Feed-Forward Network (FFN) Sub-Layer (Transformer)|FFN sub-layer]], and [[residual connection (Transformer)|residual connection + layer normalisation]].
* '''Output head''': converts the model output back into token(s), often via [[Softmax|softmax]].
